n: This chapter is a victory roll — like a monument listing defeated kings. It starts with the lands east of the Jordan, from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north.

f.g: A deep canyon flowing into the Dead Sea; Moab’s northern border.

f.w: toward the rising of the sun

n: First, Sihon the Amorite king, who ruled from Heshbon over the land between the Arnon and the Jabbok rivers.

f.g: Where Jacob wrestled with the angel.

n: Sihon’s realm also included the Jordan valley up to the Sea of Galilee and down to the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah.

f.g: The slopes of Pisgah, where Moses viewed the land.

n: Second, Og of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim (a race remembered as giants), who ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei.
Og ruled from Mount Hermon across Bashan to the borders of Geshur and Maacah, and half of Gilead.
Moses defeated these kings and gave their land to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. Joshua’s victories continue what Moses began.

f.w: Moses the servant of the LORD

n: Now the kings west of the Jordan whom Joshua defeated, from Baal-gad in the north to Mount Halak in the south.
The regions and the six peoples of Canaan are listed — the full scope of the promised land.
The list begins with the first two victories: Jericho and Ai. Each king is counted “one,” like tally marks on a scroll.
Jerusalem and Hebron — two leaders of the southern coalition. Jerusalem itself remained in Jebusite hands until David took it.
Jarmuth and Lachish, also among the five kings of chapter 10.
Eglon, and Gezer whose king died helping Lachish.
Debir and Geder in the south.
Hormah and Arad in the Negev, where Israel had fought during the wilderness years.

f.g: A town in the eastern Negev.

n: Libnah, and Adullam — where David later hid in a cave.
Makkedah, where the five kings hid, and Bethel, near Ai.
Tappuah and Hepher, towns in the central hill country.

f.g: “Apple” — a town on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh.

n: Aphek and Lasharon, on the coastal plain of Sharon.

f.g: A city where the Philistines later camped before capturing the ark.

n: Now the northern kings: Madon and Hazor.
Shimron-meron and Achshaph, allies of Jabin.
Taanach and Megiddo, guarding the great Jezreel valley. Megiddo’s name lies behind “Armageddon.”
Kedesh in Galilee and Jokneam near Mount Carmel.

f.g: A mountain ridge on the coast, later the site of Elijah’s contest.

n: Dor on the coast, and the king of “the nations of Gilgal” — possibly a different Gilgal, or Galilee of the nations.
Tirzah, later a capital of the northern kingdom. Total: thirty-one kings — each one a witness to God’s faithfulness.

f.w: all the kings thirty and one
